previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cerebrovascular disease, coronary artery disease, and alcohol use was admitted for chest pain and dizziness. Initial evaluation ruled out acute cardiac ischemia with normal troponins and EKG. The chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal. A non-contrast head CT showed no acute intracranial abnormalities, and his dizziness, described as lightheadedness, resolved with IV rehydration and was attributed to dehydration and alcohol use. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal using the CIWA protocol and received thiamine, folic acid, and multivitamins. His tremor remained at baseline, and no new neurological deficits were found. He was discharged stable with instructions to avoid alcohol, continue all prescribed medications, and follow up with primary care, with plans for home support services.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  A ___ male with chest pain.  Please evaluate for infiltrate,
effusion, or mediastinal abnormality.

FINDINGS:  A single AP portable upright chest radiograph is reviewed and
compared to ___.

Cardiomediastinal appearance is little changed, with evidence of prior median
sternotomy and CABG.  Atelectasis or scarring at the left base is unchanged. 
Lungs are otherwise clear.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. 
Pulmonary vascularity is normal.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.  Chronic atelectasis or
scarring at the left base.

HISTORY:  ___ male with atypical chest pain, intermittent x1 week. The
pain described as being under left breast, sharp, worse with lying down.
Positive ETOH.  Positive D-dimer.  Please evaluate for PE, dissection or rib
fracture.

COMPARISON:  Chest x-ray from same day, and from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT acquired axial imaging of the chest was performed before and
after administration of intravenous contrast via non-gated chest pain CTA
technique.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained and reviewed.

CTA CHEST:  There is no pulmonary embolism.  Thoracic aorta is normal in
caliber and contour throughout, without evidence of dissection.

Heart, pericardium and great vessels are normal.  There is no pleural or
pericardial effusion.  There is three-vessel coronary artery calcification.
Note is made of a dominant right vertebral artery with a diminutive left
vertebral artery. There is evidence of prior median sternotomy.

Multiple borderline enlarged small lymph nodes are seen scattered throughout
the mediastinum, and there is a likely calcified lymph node seen just superior
to the top of the aortic arch adjacent to the trachea, although this could
also represent volume averaging from adjacent aortic arch calcification.

There is streaky airspace opacity at the left lung base, which could represent
atelectasis versus aspiration, versus early infectious process.  There is mild
centrilobular emphysema, most prominent in the right upper lobe.  There is
mild right basilar atelectasis.

Limited views of the upper abdomen are notable for marked diffuse fatty
infiltration of the liver.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No suspicious lesions are seen.  There is no fracture.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No pulmonary embolism.  No aortic dissection.  No rib fractures.
2.  Streaky left basilar opacity could be consistent with atelectasis,
aspiration, or early infectious process.
3.  Three-vessel coronary artery calcifications.
4.  Multiple borderline enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes.
5.  Diffuse fatty infiltration of the liver.
